title: Jamestown Holiday Guide
intro: Everything for the holidays on the island and just over the bridges, from Thanksgiving week through New Year’s Day: times, addresses, prices and what to expect.

sections.label: Saturday, Dec. 5: The Island's Big Holiday Day

items.where: Church at Four Corners (Central Baptist Church)
items.note: The church’s yearly fair at the Four Corners opens the day. In past years it has offered gift baskets, fresh evergreen wreaths, baked goods, a Re-gift Table and handmade gifts from more than a dozen Rhode Island crafters.
items.more: Last year’s lunch menu was soup, chili and hot dogs. The church calendar lists 9 to 2 this year; last year’s fair closed at 1, so come early for the wreaths.

items.t: Friends of the Library Winter Book Sale
items.note: The Friends of the library hold their seasonal book sale on Stroll day, a good stop for stocking-stuffer books.
The Chamber of Commerce’s Stroll fills the village with business open houses, holiday sales and treats, window displays, and craft fairs at local churches and schools.
items.more: Shops and fairs keep their own hours. Chamber: 401-423-3650.

items.note: A juried market of one-of-a-kind work by local artists and artisans: ceramics, jewelry, textiles, paintings, prints and more.
items.more: Bring a canned good or shelf-stable food for the Martin Luther King Jr. Community Center in Newport; bins are in the lobby. The building is wheelchair accessible.

items.note: The lighthouse museum and gift shop reopen for holiday shopping: lighthouse ornaments, mugs and books.
items.addr: Beavertail State Park, Beavertail Road, Jamestown
items.more: Also open Dec 6, 12 and 13. Museum phone: 401-423-3270.

items.t: Santa and Mrs. Claus Arrive by Boat
items.note: The Coastal Queen docks at East Ferry at 1 p.m. sharp. Santa and Mrs. Claus then ride a fire truck up to the Conanicut Gift Shop for visits and photos from 1 to 2 p.m.
items.addr: 1 East Ferry Wharf; photos at Conanicut Gift Shop, 20 Narragansett Ave.
items.more: Get to the wharf a little before 1 to see the boat come in.

items.t: Holiday Cruise with the Very Merry Dickens Carolers
items.note: Right after Santa docks, the Coastal Queen heads back out for a 75-minute cruise with the Dickens Carolers singing traditional carols. The center bar serves holiday drinks, beer, wine and soft drinks.
items.price: Newport sailings: $44 adults, $39 seniors and military, $34 children
items.more: Book with Coastal Queen Cruises: 401-423-9900.

items.note: The town tree lights up at East Ferry, with live music and Boy Scout Troop 1 luminaries along the seawall and Narragansett Avenue.
items.addr: East Ferry Wharf, Conanicus Ave., Jamestown
items.more: It is right on the water, so dress warmly.

items.note: Sparkling Lights at The Breakers pairs a half-mile outdoor light walk with a visit inside the decorated Newport mansion. The experience runs on selected evenings from November 21 through December 27, with listed hours of 4 to 8 p.m, allowing visitors to see both the grounds and the house during the same outing. Admission is ticketed, and the season dates do not mean it operates every night. Select an available date and timed entry before traveling.

items.t: Holidays at the Newport Mansions open
items.note: Christmas decorations fill The Breakers, Marble House and Chateau-sur-Mer during Holidays at the Newport Mansions, whose season runs November 21 through January 3. Trees, wreaths, flowers and period table settings give each house a seasonal presentation within its historic rooms. Visitors can plan a mansion visit during the day and consider the separately ticketed Sparkling Lights experience at The Breakers on selected evenings. Consult the Preservation Society’s calendar for house hours, admission and holiday closures.
items.addr: The Breakers, 44 Ochre Point Ave.; Marble House, 596 Bellevue Ave.; Chateau-sur-Mer, 474 Bellevue Ave.

items.note: Rosecliff becomes part of the performance when Newport Contemporary Ballet presents The Newport Nutcracker. Rather than keeping the entire audience in a conventional theater setting, the production moves through the mansion and includes a Newport-themed second act, connecting the ballet’s holiday story with the city around it. Admission is for ages 6 and older, with tickets listed from $159.

items.t: A Rough Point Holiday: After Dark
items.note: Doris Duke’s oceanfront house decorated for the season and open after dark, with warm drinks and jazz.

Decorated boats take their holiday displays onto Newport Harbor for the Illuminated Boat Parade on November 27 at 6:00 p.m. Crews compete for the best display, turning the harbor itself into the setting for the evening’s celebration. The event is listed as free to watch, giving visitors an outdoor holiday option along the Newport waterfront. Check the organizer’s latest announcement for viewing guidance and weather-related changes before making the trip.

Santa joins a free holiday gathering at the Shops at Long Wharf in Newport on November 28, from 4 to 6 p.m. The program includes a tree lighting, music, children’s crafts, letters to Santa and photo opportunities, bringing several family activities into a single late-afternoon visit. The rain date is November 29, which is an alternative date rather than a second scheduled celebration. Check the organizer’s announcement if the forecast affects the event.

Newport Harbor Island Resort celebrates its Lighting of the Lighthouse on November 28 at 5:00 p.m, with carolers and seasonal decorations accompanying the public gathering. Hot chocolate for children and cider are included in the event description, adding refreshments to the waterfront holiday tradition. The lighthouse lighting offers an early-evening stop for visitors already exploring Newport’s seasonal celebrations; confirm the resort’s latest event arrangements before arriving.

items.t: Candy Cane Express Cruise with Mrs. Claus
items.note: One-hour family sailings from Jamestown with Mrs. Claus aboard for the little ones.
items.more: Book with Coastal Queen Cruises: 401-423-9900.

items.note: A holiday brunch with Santa on Goat Island.

sections.label: On the Island: Concerts, Parties and Shopping

items.t: Holiday Arts Market Pre-Party and Early Shopping
items.note: First pick of the market the night before the Stroll.
More afternoons to shop the lighthouse gift shop, closed since fall.
items.more: Ask about the Beavertail charity license plate: $43.50 a set, $20 of it to the lighthouse.

items.t: A Contemporary Christmas: Jamestown Community Chorus
items.note: The island’s chorus, founded in 1949, sings a holiday program of mostly 21st-century music with a few folk tunes.
items.more: Chorus contact: 401-787-4487.

items.t: Narragansett Café Annual Christmas Party with The Renegades
items.note: The Ganny’s yearly Christmas party, with Amber Rose and The Renegades.

items.t: Christmas Eve at the Island Churches
items.note: St. Matthew’s Episcopal, Central Baptist and St. Mark Catholic all hold Christmas services; each posts its Christmas Eve and Christmas Day times in December.
items.addr: St. Matthew’s, 87 Narragansett Ave.; Central Baptist, 99 Narragansett Ave.; St. Mark, 60 Narragansett Ave.
items.more: We will add the times here as the churches post them.

items.note: Families make their own hanukkiah, with PJ Library and Harbor Creative Arts.
items.price: $18 per family, kit included; extra kits $18
items.more: Register by Nov 22.

items.note: A two-hour workshop with Petra Napolitano to sew your own stuffed ornaments.
items.more: Ages 13 and up; younger children with a parent. Registration required.

items.t: Wreath Decorating Workshop at Mount Hope Farm
items.note: An evening wreath-decorating workshop in the farm’s barn.
items.more: Confirm price and registration with the farm.

items.note: Make a fresh wreath with the Preservation Society’s greenhouse staff.

items.t: Cookie Decorating and Spanish Fun with Solé
items.note: Kids practice beginner Spanish while decorating two cookies to take home.
items.more: Kindergarten through grade 4. Registration required.

sections.label: Over the Bridge in Newport and Middletown

items.t: On the Farce Day of Christmas
items.note: Ken Levine’s holiday comedy: a divorced daughter pays her ex to play husband at her parents’ house in Utah for Christmas.
items.more: Play and dinner packages available; check the Playhouse for times.

items.note: Author Lisa Goddard signs her children’s holiday book.
A visit with Santa, co-hosted with Lorelei’s for Littles.
items.more: Time not listed; check before you go.

items.note: Newport’s month-long Christmas celebration, running every December since 1971, with events nearly every day.
items.more: It traditionally opens with the Washington Square tree lighting, a proclamation from the mayor and a Newport Artillery cannon salute.

items.t: Luminaria and Festival of Lights at Salve Regina
items.note: About 1,000 luminarias at Our Lady of Mercy Chapel and the 24th annual multi-faith Festival of Lights at Ochre Court, with music, dance and prayers.
Holiday shopping inside the historic Colony House.

Bowen’s Wharf celebrates its 56th annual Christmas tree lighting in Newport on December 5, with festivities beginning around 12:30 p.m. and the tree illuminated at 6 p.m. Santa, live music, local musicians and choruses fill the afternoon program before the evening lighting. Santa and Mrs. Claus are expected to arrive by boat if the weather allows, adding a harbor arrival to the wharf’s celebration. Admission is free; check the organizer’s program for the final sequence of activities.

The low voices of Cantus fill Emmanuel Church in Newport with Christmas music on December 5 at 3:30 p.m. The concert pairs familiar carols with contemporary choral works, offering listeners both recognizable seasonal melodies and newer music written for voices. Its focus is the ensemble’s singing and the holiday repertoire, making this an afternoon option for readers looking for a concert rather than a market or outdoor festival. See Newport Classical for tickets and seating information.
Handel’s Messiah in the Rosecliff ballroom, sung by Ensemble Altera and the Professional Choristers of the Choir School of Newport County.

Whitehall Museum House in Middletown opens for a colonial-style Christmas gathering on December 6, from 1 to 3 p.m. Decorations, live music and a traditional wassail bowl form part of the afternoon, with festive treats prepared by the Colonial Dames. The program offers a smaller historic-house celebration, centered on seasonal customs and hospitality rather than a large commercial light display. See the event announcement for visitor and admission information.

items.t: Glen Manor House Christmas Open House
items.note: Glen Manor House opens its doors for its Christmas Open House on December 6, from 1:30 to 4 p.m. The visit offers an opportunity to see the house dressed for the holidays during a seasonal public opening, rather than attending a private function there. Check Glen Manor’s own announcement for admission arrangements and any visitor instructions, especially if combining the afternoon with another East Bay holiday stop.
A morning tour of how the mansions are decorated for the holidays.

items.t: The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas
items.note: The Irish Tenors bring their family Christmas show to Washington Square.

items.t: Pictures with Santa and ‘A Visit from St. Nicholas’
items.note: Photos with Santa, with readings of the poem at noon, 12:30 and 1, plus a Spanish-language reading at 1:30.
items.more: RSVP recommended.

items.t: Christmas Open House, Museum of Newport Irish History
items.note: The Museum of Newport Irish History holds its 10th annual Christmas Open House on December 12, offering a seasonal visit to the museum during Newport’s holiday program. The event combines the museum setting with a Christmas gathering, providing an alternative to the larger outdoor festivals and performances. Check the museum’s announcement for opening hours, admission and the ornament details mentioned in the listing before planning a stop.

Frisson brings a chamber-music Christmas program to Emmanuel Church in Newport. Selections from The Nutcracker and Vivaldi’s Winter share the program with “Carol of the Bells” and a Christmas sing-along, moving between classical concert music and familiar seasonal favorites. Two performances are listed that afternoon. Check Newport Classical’s booking calendar for the 1:00 p.m. performance before purchasing, since the linked series page may open on another seating.

items.t: Holiday Cruises with the Dickens Carolers from Newport
items.note: 75-minute caroling cruises on the Coastal Queen.
items.price: $44 adults; $39 seniors and military; $34 children and youth

items.note: Santa joins passengers aboard the Coastal Queen for a Newport meet-and-greet cruise. The approximately one-hour outing combines time with Santa, hot chocolate and holiday music aboard a decorated boat, taking a familiar seasonal visit onto the water. Confirm the departure point, ticket availability and any weather-related arrangements with the cruise operator.

items.t: A Musical Retelling of ‘A Christmas Carol’ with Christine Baranski
items.note: One night only: the vocal ensemble Skylark sings the story, narrated by actress Christine Baranski.

items.t: A Christmas Carol at Trinity Rep
items.note: Trinity Rep’s annual A Christmas Carol returns to the Dowling Theater at 201 Washington Street in Providence for its 50th-anniversary production, with the run continuing through December 31. Dickens’s story follows Ebenezer Scrooge through the Christmas encounters that change his view of the people around him. Choose a specific date and showtime through Trinity Rep’s ticket calendar.

items.t: Christmas Preparations with the 1910 Household Staff
items.note: Costumed household staff show how the manor got ready for a 1910 Christmas, then you tour the decorated house on your own.
items.more: Two timed sessions; check Blithewold for tickets.

items.note: The Bristol mansion decorated room by room, with the evening Sparkle! light display on the grounds.
items.more: Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.

items.t: ’Twas the Night Before… by Cirque du Soleil
items.note: Acrobatics, dance and Christmas music bring a familiar holiday poem to the stage when Cirque du Soleil presents ’Twas the Night Before… at PPAC in Providence. The family production combines its Christmas characters and story with the company’s physical performance style, offering a holiday outing built around movement and spectacle. PPAC advertises a family-ticket offer involving a child age 18 or younger and a regularly priced ticket; check the box office for the current terms and available seats.

items.t: Holiday Jazz Tea with Chelley Knight’s Quartet
items.note: Live jazz with afternoon tea in the manor dining room.
items.more: Rain date Nov 29.

items.note: Make a holiday wreath with Blithewold’s horticulture team.
items.more: Check Blithewold for supplies and price.

items.note: Wickford begins its 41st annual Festival of Lights with the official tree lighting at Updike Park. The opening brings the village into a four-day holiday program that continues through December 6 with shopping, music and family activities. Visitors can make the tree lighting their first stop in the village celebration, but should check the organizer’s final schedule for the ceremony time and other opening-night activities.

South Kingstown’s Festival of Trees brings decorated trees together with seasonal activities during a December 4–January 3 run. The listing describes children’s activities, caroling, music, cocoa and handmade local gifts, combining things to see with opportunities to shop and gather. Confirm the venue and operating calendar with the organizer.

Bristol gathers for its Grand Illumination on December 5 near the Burnside Building at Hope and Court streets, where the town’s Christmas tree lighting anchors the celebration. Local school performers and other holiday festivities are part of the program, connecting the downtown decorations with a community gathering. The rain date is December 6. Check the town’s final announcement for the program’s start time and any weather-related move to the alternate date.

items.t: Music in the Living Room at Blithewold
items.note: Holiday music in the decorated manor: mezzo-soprano Nancy Hood on Dec 12 and jazz pianist Laszlo Gardony on Dec 13.
items.price: Ticket includes manor and grounds admission
items.more: Registration required to reserve a seat.

items.t: Boston Pops Holiday Concert with Keith Lockhart
items.note: Keith Lockhart and the Boston Pops bring their holiday concert to PPAC in Providence, with a program that includes “Sleigh Ride,” seasonal arrangements and a sing-along. A visit from Santa is part of the festivities, giving the orchestral concert a family element alongside its music. There are afternoon and evening performances on the same day, so check the selected showtime carefully when reserving seats through PPAC.

Clara’s Christmas Eve adventure unfolds to Tchaikovsky’s score when Ballet Rhode Island performs The Nutcracker at The VETS in Providence. Company artists share the stage with local young performers in the holiday ballet, bringing together its Christmas story, classical dancing and familiar music. Tickets are listed from $36 through the company’s official ticket providers. Selected matinees offer a post-show “Meet the Stars” experience; check whether it is attached to this performance when booking.

sections.label: New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day

items.note: Charlestown’s New Year’s Eve Bonfire is listed for December 31, from 4:30 to 7 p.m, at Ninigret Park, 5 Park Lane. The gathering centers on a community bonfire, offering an outdoor early-evening alternative to a late-night dinner or party. The page does not establish admission, age restrictions or a fuller program. Confirm the town or organizer’s current announcement, including weather arrangements, before heading to the park.

items.t: Providence New Year’s Eve Celebration and Illuminate PVD Fireworks
items.where: 195 District Park and the Van Leesten Pedestrian Bridge
items.note: Providence’s New Year’s Eve celebration brings music, food and family activities to 195 District Park and the Michael Van Leesten Memorial Pedestrian Bridge on December 31, from 5 to 9 p.m. The free, all-ages gathering combines entertainment and illuminated installations before an 8:30 p.m. fireworks show over the river.

items.t: Holiday Lights Spectacular on New Year’s Eve
items.note: Roger Williams Park Zoo’s Holiday Lights Spectacular welcomes New Year’s Eve visitors on December 31, from 5 to 9:30 p.m, at 1000 Elmwood Avenue in Providence. The walking route covers 40 acres and is described as featuring more than 3.5 million lights, making the displays the focus of the evening visit. Advance online tickets are required; a later listing gives a $13–$15 range. Confirm the price for the selected entry time when booking.

The Chanler’s “The Scarlet House” combines a crimson-themed reception with dinner and dancing on December 31, from 7 p.m. to 1 a.m, at 117 Memorial Boulevard in Newport. Live modern violin leads into a four-course meal, followed by a DJ, late-night bites and a midnight toast. The price is $385 plus service charge and tax. Reserve directly and confirm the current menu, dress guidance and total price.

items.t: Newport Harbor Island Resort New Year’s Eve
items.note: Newport Harbor Island Resort has announced a New Year’s Eve celebration on Goat Island for December 31, from 8:30 p.m. to 1 a.m. Check the resort’s updated event page before booking so that the ticket inclusions, dining arrangements and program are clear, rather than assuming a particular band or dinner format.

A Wish Come True’s 23rd Annual Polar Plunge Challenge brings “Freezin’ for a Reason” to Easton’s Beach in Newport on January 1. The plunge begins at noon sharp at 175 Memorial Boulevard, with a listed event window extending to 1:30 p.m. Spectators are welcome as well as participants, and participation begins with a $25 donation. Register through the organizer and check its arrival instructions before heading to the beach.
